newsitem.title: USA: NYC sues tobacco industry over health care costs.
newsitem.headline: NYC sues tobacco industry over health care costs.

text.p: New York City sued major tobacco companies Thursday in an effort to recoup Medicaid costs of treating lung cancer and other diseases.

The suit, filed in New York State Supreme Court in Manhattan, seeks unspecified actual and punitive damages to be determined at trial. The suit alleges, among other things, that the industry violated the New York State's law on deceptive trade practices.

Defendants in the suit include Philip Morris Cos Inc ; RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp's R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co; B.A.T Industries Plc's Brown & Williamson Tobacco Corp;Brooke Group Ltd's Liggett Group Inc, and Loews Corp's Lorillard Tobacco Co Inc.
The suit also names the Tobacco Institute and the Council for Tobacco Research Inc.
The tobacco industry criticized New York City Mayor Rudolph Giuliani for bringing the suit.
"It would appear that Mayor Giuliani has conferred only with rabid antismokers and product liability lawyers before filing today's suit," said R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co in a statement.

"We regret that he didn't ask the tobacco industry at the very least to sit down and discuss the litigation before suing us," Reynolds said, adding that it believed there was a serious question about whether Giuliani has jurisdiction to bring such a case.
"The mayor may garner some political mileage out of this filing, but that will be all," Reynolds said.
The City said earlier it was seeking to recover certain costs of treating Medicaid patients and uninsured patience treated without charge in public hospitals.
It also said in a statement earlier that it will try to recoup the medical expenses incurred by its employees.
Similar lawsuits have been filed against the tobacco industry by 16 states.
